patients.label: 81-year-old woman with complete heart block complicating takotsubo syndrome

identity_evidence.quote: An 81-year-old woman presents with shortness of breath resulting in a diagnosis of picornavirus and complete heart block.

attribution_limitations: The discussion says the Takotsubo syndrome appears to have been precipitated by the lower respiratory tract infection with picornavirus; this is the authors' hedged inference.

The authors state it is unclear when complete heart block developed and that the possibility of progressive conduction disease is high; the order of Takotsubo syndrome and heart block is not established.
The coughing and agitation on lying flat could be attributed to either heart failure or respiratory tract infection; the chest X-ray was not consistent with heart failure.

The text places the echocardiogram after transfer, whereas the Figure 2 caption says the transthoracic echocardiogram was performed on presentation; it is not stated whether these are the same study or whether presentation means the first or tertiary hospital.
The text describes near normalisation of the apical hypokinesis on the left ventriculogram, whereas the Figure 3 caption says resolution of the apical hypokinesis.
The text reports high sensitivity troponin 525 ng/L and Table 1 lists Troponin I 525 as the initial value; the source does not say they are the same measurement.

Table 2 row 24 (the article's first author, 2020, 81, F, CIED Yes, 3 months follow-up, not resolved) has no citation and matches 'Including our case', but the table never labels it as this patient; its 3-month follow-up differs from the text's 6 months following discharge.

Medications are listed under the 'Medications at Admission' section heading; the sentence itself does not state they were taken or continued in hospital, and discharge medications are listed without doses.
